quantity: reduction from baseline of circulating CD4+ T-cell count
dose: 12 mg/m2 every 3 months (the regimen of the only fetched longitudinal 12-month study)
timepoint: month 12 sought; none found with a number
source: none stating a number. Nearest fetched: Chanvillard C et al. 2012, PLoS One 7(6):e39625 (SPMS, n=12 completers, sampled at baseline, 6 and 12 months, each 3 months after the previous infusion)
quote: MX treatment did not affect the populations of CD14+ monocytes, CD4+ Th or conventional CD8high T cells at these time points (Figure 1B).
note: No fetched source gives an absolute CD4+ count (or a percent change of it) at or near 12 months on an MS regimen. The quoted sentence is qualitative, refers to whole-blood population frequencies shown only as a figure, and is a trough sample 3 months after dosing; it was NOT converted to an anchor of 0. Abstracts only (full text paywalled, not read): Gbadamosi 2003 Eur Neurol (PMID 12646755) reports a reduction of most lymphocyte subsets at day 14 with only the B-cell decrease persisting, CD4/CD8 ratio unchanged, no numbers in the abstract; Pelfrey 2006 J Neuroimmunol (PMID 16644023, PPMS, 9 months) reports no selective loss of CD4 cells; a 2009 Eur Neurol study (PMID 18948697) gives ~30% B-cell reduction only. Tried: PubMed (4 query variants, about 80 records screened by title/abstract), Exa web search, DailyMed mitoxantrone label (no CD4 or subset data), publisher pages for Gbadamosi and Pelfrey (HTTP 403 / not open access per Unpaywall), Europe PMC full-text search (service returned 503). No Millefiorini-regimen (8 mg/m2 monthly) immunophenotyping source was found.

quantity: alpha-4 integrin (VLA-4) receptor saturation/occupancy at trough
note: No fetched source states a receptor occupancy or saturation figure for firategrast at any dose. Tried: PubMed ('firategrast OR SB-683699', all 10 records screened), ClinicalTrials.gov API for all 6 firategrast studies (no occupancy/saturation outcome, none with posted results), two Exa web searches, Grove 2013 Eur J Neurol abstract (PMID 23419064; blood lymphocyte counts 'elevated' at weeks 4 and 24 at this dose, no number, no occupancy). Full texts of Miller 2012 Lancet Neurol (PMID 22226929) and Grove 2013 are paywalled (HTTP 403, not open access) and were not read; if an occupancy figure exists it is most likely in the Miller 2012 dose rationale or a GSK study report. Disclosure: search results and the Miller 2012 abstract displayed lesion outcomes for this trial; they were not used for anything in this file.

quantity: BTK occupancy in PBMC at trough (predose), steady state; population PK/PD model simulation, reported as share of patients above a threshold
source: Papasouliotis O et al. 2022, Clin Transl Sci 15(12):2888-2898, Table 4 and text (model built on phase II RMS patient data, fasted; 1000 simulated patients per regimen)
quote: evobrutinib dose of 45 mg b.i.d. with food is predicted to achieve similar efficacy (predose BTKO of >95% in 93% of patients) as 75 mg b.i.d. while fasted
note: Capped: raw value is a threshold statement (>0.95), entered as 0.95. Simulated, not measured, at 45 mg b.i.d. fed; Table 4 same regimen: 99% of simulated patients above 0.90, 100% above 0.80. Observed support in the same paper (Table 1, RMS patients, 75 mg b.i.d. fasted, stated to give similar exposure): predose BTKO above 0.95 in 98% of patients, above 0.90 in 100%. Healthy-volunteer model (Papasouliotis 2022, PMID 36165192, PMC9747113, Table 4): 50 mg b.i.d. fed, minimum BTKO above 0.95 in 85% and above 0.90 in 99%. No median or mean trough occupancy is given for 45 mg b.i.d. The source is an exposure-response paper; only the PK/BTKO simulation was used, no efficacy result entered the choice of value.

quantity: mean BTK occupancy in PBMC 24 h after the day-10 dose (trough of a once-daily regimen), normalised to day-1 predose
source: Owens TD et al. 2022, Clin Transl Sci 15(2):442-450, Table 4 (phase 1 MAD, part B)
note: Healthy volunteers (flag), not MS patients; 8 per cohort (6 active, 2 placebo). Table columns: placebo, 7.5, 15, 30, 60, 90 mg; values are percent occupancy mean ± SD. Day 10 may be short of full steady state for a covalent inhibitor, though day-1 24 h occupancy at 60 mg was already 93 ± 2. Same table, 60 mg: day 10 4 h 96 ± 1, 48 h 85 ± 3. Measured directly at the stated dose.

raw_value: >=0.90 (IC90 maintained over the whole dosing interval in >75% of patients, model projection)
quantity: stated target inhibition, not occupancy: functional BTK inhibition (PK/PD model on phase 1 biomarkers, BTK autophosphorylation in B cells and CD63 on basophils), expressed as plasma concentration at or above IC90 through trough
timepoint: entire dosing interval incl. trough, steady state (projected)
source: Metz M et al. 2021, Nat Med 27(11):1961-1969, Methods dose rationale (citing the healthy-volunteer phase 1 PK/PD model, Herman 2018)
quote: the 200 mg twice daily dose was expected to provide a steady-state exposure achieving 90% maximal inhibitory concentration over the entire dosing interval in >75% of patients
note: Weak. Fenebrutinib is non-covalent, so no probe-based occupancy exists; the measure is model-projected functional inhibition, a lower bound (>=90% in >75% of patients), secondary citation of a model built in healthy volunteers (flag) and stated in a urticaria trial's methods. Not measured at 200 mg b.i.d.: the phase 1 MAD (Herman 2018, PMID 29484638, abstract only, full text paywalled) dosed up to 250 mg b.i.d. Same Nat Med paper gives 'approximately 70-90%' for the three trial regimens together; Chan P et al. 2020 (Pharm Res 37(2):25, PMC6944649) says '70 to 90% BTK inhibition over the dosing interval in the majority of patients' across 50 mg q.d. to 200 mg b.i.d. If the 70-90% range were read as applying to 200 mg b.i.d. the midpoint would be 0.80; 0.90 was entered because it is the only statement specific to this dose. Isenberg 2021 (SLE, PMID 34042314, read as a search-result excerpt of the publisher page) reports mean steady-state predose concentrations of 137-197 ng/mL at 200 mg b.i.d. with pBTK reductions shown only in a supplementary figure.

quantity: Teff: reduction from baseline of absolute count of circulating CD4+ effector memory T cells (CD3+CD4+CD45RO+CCR7-), derived from absolute CD4+ count change x fold change of Tem share of CD4+
dose: 2 mg/day assumed (EXPAND trial arm; dose not restated in the fetched text)
timepoint: 6 months and 9-12 months on treatment (midpoint of the two)
source: Wu Q et al. 2020, JCI Insight 5(3):e134251, full text read at insight.jci.org (AMS04 substudy of EXPAND, SPMS, siponimod n=14-23 depending on assay)
quote: CD4+ T cells were decreased by 97% to 25 ± 15 cells/μL at 6 months (P ≤ 0.0001) and 96% to 33 cells/μL at 9–12 months [...] Within the siponimod-treated group, the frequency of Tem was increased about 2.9-fold (P = 0.0006) and 2.5-fold (P = 0.0011) at 6 months and 9–12 months, respectively, compared with pretreatment levels
note: Converted from proportion-of-CD4 within the same paper. Arithmetic: remaining Tem fraction = (1 - CD4 reduction) x fold change in Tem share. 6 months: 0.03 x 2.9 = 0.087, reduction 0.913. 9-12 months: 0.04 x 2.5 = 0.100, reduction 0.900. Midpoint 0.907. Weak points: the paper prints percent CD4 reduction and fold changes, not baseline Tem counts; product of group means, not a paired per-patient mean; CD4 counts gated TCRab+CD4+ (n up to 23/20/18), frequencies gated CD3+CD4+ (n=14/15/14); 'about' 2.9/2.5-fold is rounded, so +-0.1 fold moves the result by about 0.004; Tem is defined CD45RO+CCR7-, not CD45RA-CCR7-. The 96-97% CD4 reduction is as printed. Off-dose corroboration, not used: Gergely 2012 (PMID 22646698, PMC3485666), healthy volunteers, 10 mg/day x 28 days, median fold decrease of absolute CD4+ peripheral effector memory (CCR7-) count 8.2 (IQR 6.2-13.1) = 0.878; subset counts reported for the 10 mg group only.

quantity: Treg: reduction from baseline of absolute count of circulating regulatory T cells (CD4+CD25+FoxP3+), derived from absolute CD4+ count change x fold change of Treg share of CD4+
dose: 2 mg/day assumed (EXPAND trial arm; dose not restated in the fetched text)
timepoint: 6 months and 9-12 months on treatment (midpoint of the two)
source: Wu Q et al. 2020, JCI Insight 5(3):e134251, full text read at insight.jci.org (AMS04 substudy of EXPAND, SPMS, siponimod n=14-23 depending on assay)
quote: CD4+ T cells were decreased by 97% to 25 ± 15 cells/μL at 6 months (P ≤ 0.0001) and 96% to 33 cells/μL at 9–12 months [...] Tregs (Figure 8G) increased 2.4-fold at 6 months (P = 0.0012) and 3-fold at 9–12 months (P = 0.0026) after siponimod treatment
note: Converted from proportion-of-CD4 within the same paper. Arithmetic: remaining Treg fraction = (1 - CD4 reduction) x fold change in Treg share. 6 months: 0.03 x 2.4 = 0.072, reduction 0.928. 9-12 months: 0.04 x 3.0 = 0.120, reduction 0.880. Midpoint 0.904. Same weak points as the Teff row (fold changes and percent reduction, not tabulated counts; product of group means with different n and slightly different CD4 gates; rounded fold values: '3-fold' read as 2.5-3.5 gives 0.86-0.90 at 9-12 months). Treg and Teff anchors are within 0.01 of each other and the difference is inside this rounding error. No other fetched source gives absolute Treg counts on siponimod: Spiezia 2024 (PMID 38632126, PMC11233419) tabulates naive/memory regulatory T cells as percentages only; Gergely 2012 has no Treg.
